This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 01.02.2020 passed by the Additional Small Causes Judge and Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.7569/2017.

entities.text: Additional Small Causes Judge and Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
Hence, the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under;
That on 23.08.2017 at about 2.30 p.m., claimant was traveling on his TVS XL moped bearing No.KA-53-W-8665 on Bengaluru-Chintamani Road.

When he reached near Maruthi showroom, a car bearing registration No.KA-03-MZ-9102 came NC: 2024:KHC:1935 in a rash and negligent manner from wrong side of the road and dashed against the TVS XL moped from behind.
Due to which, claimant was knocked down and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
Thereafter, he was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopedic and Surgical Hospital at Kolar and admitted as an inpatient for six days and discharged with an advise to take follow up treatment.

entities.text: Gaurav Orthopedic and Surgical Hospital at Kolar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The claimant spent huge amount towards treatment and incidental expenses.
3.1 It is stated that the claimant was hale and healthy prior to the occurrence of accident, aged about 60 years and he was involved in agricultural work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the occurrence of accident and injuries sustained, claimant became disabled to perform his day to day agricultural activities.
Hence, he filed a claim petition seeking enhancement.

sentences.text: On service of notice, respondent No.1-owner of the offending vehicle remained absent and he was placed Ex parte.

Respondent No.2-Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition including the age,
avocation and income and magnitude of the injuries suffered so NC: 2024:KHC:1935 also the negligence attributed against the driver of the car.
Therefore, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.3 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
3.4 In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and the Doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P14.

On the other hand,
respondent No.1 got examined as RW.1 and did not mark any documents.

3.5 On the basis of materials evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.5,33,324/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit and also held that respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the claimant and respondent No.2 being the insurer was directed to deposit the amount within 90 days from the date of award.
4.
It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the compensation awarded by the tribunal is on the lower side.

The tribunal has not considered NC: 2024:KHC:1935 the material evidence placed on record so also the tribunal has not awarded reasonable compensation under the heads pain and suffering, loss of income during laid up period, loss of amenities and other heads.
Hence, he seeks to allow the appeal preferred by the claimant and seeks enhancement of compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel representing Insurance Company vehemently contends that the tribunal has awarded reasonable compensation on the basis of material evidence placed on record,
the same does not call for interference.
He also contends that under other heads also reasonable compensation has been awarded by the tribunal, which does not call for interference from the hands of this Court.
Therefore, on these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

6. Having heard learned counsel for appellant and learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company, perused the impugned judgment and award, it is not in dispute that on 23.08.2017, where the claimant was proceedings on his TVS XL moped, the driver of the offending car came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the vehicle of the claimant, leading to the accident and injuries suffered due to NC: 2024:KHC:1935 the negligence of the driver of the car.

In order to establish these aspects, the claimant has produced the documents as Exs.P1 to P14, out of which,
Exs.P1 to P6 are the police records, which evidence the fact that FIR is lodged and charge sheet has been laid against the driver of the car.
Therefore, negligence is rightly attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
In order to establish the medical expenses and injuries sustained, medical records are produced at Exs.P7 to P14.

sentences.text: The income taken by the tribunal is Rs.8,000/- per month as notional income.
No documentary proof is produced before the tribunal to show the income.
However, the notional income chart of the Legal Services Authority prescribes the income of Rs.11,000/- for the accident of the year 2017.
Accordingly, income is taken as Rs.11,000/-.
The age of the claimant was 60 years.

The tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier at '9' as contemplated in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121, which does not call for interference.
NC: 2024:KHC:1935 8.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW.2-Doctor has opined the disability of the claimant to be 26% to the whole body, the tribunal has taken the same, which also does not call for interference.
Therefore, loss of future earning capacity due to disability would be Rs.3,08,880/- (Rs.11,000/- x 12 x 9 x 26%) as against Rs.2,24,640/- awarded by the tribunal.

9. The tribunal has awarded a sum Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.50,000/-
towards conveyance, nourishment and nutritious food, the same does not call for interference.
10. Towards medical expenses, Rs.1,48,684/- is awarded by the tribunal on the basis of bills produced by the claimants.
Hence, the same also does not call for interference.
11. Towards loss of amenities, tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/-.
This Court deems it appropriate to award an additional amount of Rs.20,000/-.

In all, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.50,000/-
under this head.
12. Towards future medical expenses, PW.2-Doctor has opined that Rs.80,000/- would be required to the claimant, whereas, the tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/-.
This Court NC: 2024:KHC:1935 deems it appropriate to award an additional amount of Rs.20,000/-.
In all, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.50,000/- under this head.
13. The tribunal has failed to award any compensation under the head loss of income during laid up period.

The claimant having sustained fractures and disability to an extent of 26% and in view of this Court enhancing the income of the claimant to Rs.11,000/- from Rs.8,000/-, claimant would require at least four months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.44,000/- (Rs.11,000/- x 4) under the head loss of earning during laid up period.

14. In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,01,564/- as against Rs.5,33,324/- as mentioned in the table below:
